query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a secondary phase, specifically a coherent L1₂ (Ni₃Fe) precipitate, into the single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy will increase the coercive field by pinning domain walls, thereby overcoming the coercivity limitation.
generation.intervention: Introduction of a coherent L1₂ (Ni₃Fe) precipitate secondary phase through aging treatment at 500°C for 10 hours
generation.conditions: Aging treatment at 500°C for 10 hours to form coherent L1₂ precipitates, followed by water quenching to room temperature
generation.mechanism: Pinning of domain walls by the coherent L1₂ precipitates, increasing the energy required for domain wall motion and thus increasing the coercive field
generation.predicted_outcome: Increase in coercive field by at least 50% relative to the single-phase fcc FeCoNi baseline (from 100 Oe to 150 Oe)
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy with a coercive field of 100 Oe
generation.boundary: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with fcc structure and potential secondary phases, measured through magnetic hysteresis loops
generation.uncertainty: The size and distribution of the L1₂ precipitates may affect the pinning efficiency and thus the coercive field, and the aging treatment conditions may need to be optimized

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare and characterize FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with and without the introduction of a secondary phase (L1₂ precipitates) through aging treatment, and measure their magnetic properties using hysteresis loops
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the alloy with the introduced secondary phase is not significantly increased (>150 Oe) compared to the baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

frame.system: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its high-entropy alloy derivatives
frame.limitation: Low coercive field (no greater than 100 Oe)
prior_attempts: reported magnetic measurements on single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys

intervention_hypothesis.mechanism: Pinning of domain walls or reduction of grain size to increase coercivity
intervention_hypothesis.predicted_change: Increased coercive field relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its derivatives

controlled_experiment.falsification_criterion: No significant increase in coercive field (>100 Oe) is observed with the introduction of a secondary phase or grain refinement
